❯ In the stock list, allow me to click on any item and open the same screen we see when we scan a product
  barcode, and we are able to set its quantity and expiry date. Actually we are allowing people to edit the
  quanitity and expiry date of an item. When the screen opens, by default it will show the quanitty of that

content.text:
The flow makes sense for the common case, but the single-counter-delta has one ambiguity worth resolving up front: if someone edits 10 → 8 because of a counting correction (not a dispense), it'll get logged as "2 dispensed" and pollute your dispense analytics. I'd suggest the screen open the same way, but ask the user to pick an intent — **Add**, **Dispense**, or **Correct** — before the counter does anything; default to whichever is most common (probably Dispense) so it's still one tap for the normal case.

The other thing to think about is **expiry**: when stock is *added*, it's usually a new batch with a new expiry, not an edit of the existing one — so on "Add" the expiry field should accept a new date and you'll eventually want batch tracking (FEFO dispensing). On "Dispense" and "Correct", expiry should stay read-only. Want me to go with the intent-selector version, or keep it simpler with just add/dispense and skip "correct" for now?

message.content: since our users are not that tech savvy and that much literate, lets keep the seperation of concern, items will only be dispensed from the dispense section, it will only be added using the scan option which internally has option for barcode, manual barcode or no barcode, in no barcode, if a user selects an item which is already linked to a barcode, show them directly the screen which we show when a barcode is matched to a product, the screen to enter quantity and expiry. now coming to the stock list, any changes done in the stock list would be a correction. not dispense, not addition, a correction. analyze this plan, give me any suggestion or advice you have, then after my confirmation, imeplement it.

content.text:
The separation is clean and matches user literacy well — three sections, three intents, no mode-switching inside a screen. A few things worth deciding before I code:

1. **Label and visual treatment.** Call it "Correct stock" (not "Edit") on the screen so it's clear this isn't normal add/dispense. Consider a subtle warning color or icon so users feel the friction — corrections should be the rare path, not the lazy shortcut for "I don't want to scan."

2. **Audit trail.** Corrections are the most abuse-prone action (someone covers shrinkage by "correcting" 50 → 30). Log every correction with: who, when, old qty, new qty, old expiry, new expiry, and ideally a **required reason** dropdown (Damaged / Expired-discarded / Miscount / Other+note). This is cheap to build now and impossible to backfill later.

3. **"No barcode → item already linked" case.** Good catch in your plan. Confirm the UX: when they pick an already-linked item, do we just silently route to the quantity/expiry screen, or show a tiny "this item has a barcode — next time you can scan" hint? I'd lean toward the silent route (less friction) but it's worth a one-line nudge eventually.

4. **Expiry on correction.** Should correcting let them change expiry? Yes — that's the whole point of "correction" — but if your model is one-expiry-per-item, a correction overwrites batch history. Fine for now; flag for later when batches come in.

5. **Negative/zero corrections.** Allow 0 (item fully consumed/lost). Disallow negative. Confirm whether "correct to 0" should also unlink/remove the item or just leave it at 0.

If you're good with (1) styling as a clear "Correction" action, (2) **required reason dropdown + audit log**, (3) silent route on no-barcode→linked, and (5) min=0, I'll implement. Want the reason dropdown in, or skip it for v1?

content.content:
# field-app

The **warehouse / floor mobile app** for inventory and asset operations. Android-first, distributed internally via EAS. Built for staff on low-to-mid-end phones with patchy Wi-Fi — offline-first by design.

> Root context: see `../CLAUDE.md` for the product vision and the four constraints (cost, literacy, device capability, infrastructure) that govern all design decisions.
> Long-form dev setup (toolchain, EAS, Android Studio): see `DEVELOPMENT.md` in this folder.

## What this app does

- On-the-floor inventory and asset scanning (barcode / QR via `react-native-vision-camera`)
- Offline-first: local SQLite (`expo-sqlite`), syncs with backend when network returns
- Haptics + camera + network-aware UX (`expo-haptics`, `expo-network`)
- Designed for warehouse/staff phones, not for office admins (that's `ops-dashboard`) or visitors (that's `visitor-web`)

Stack: **Expo SDK 54 + React Native 0.81 + React 19 + TypeScript + React Navigation + expo-sqlite + vision-camera**. Pinned to **Node 22 LTS** (Node 24 breaks Expo's config-plugin loader).

## Why native and not PWA?

The `visitor-web` PWA works because it lives on a fixed tablet on Wi-Fi. The field app needs:

- Reliable offline operation (warehouse Wi-Fi is patchy)
- Native barcode scanning performance
- Hardware-level camera focus control
- Background sync when network returns

PWAs cannot do these well enough. See `../PWA_vs_Native_Decision.md` at repo root.

## Commands

```bash
# Day-to-day JS/TS changes (Metro hot-reloads in <1s)
npm start                  # Expo dev server, expects an installed dev-client APK on the device

# Rebuild dev-client (only when native code / plugins / native libs change)
npm run start:dev-client   # Dev server pointed at dev-client builds
npm run android            # Local rebuild via Android Studio (requires Java 17, ANDROID_HOME)
npm run prebuild           # Regenerate native /android folder from app.json

npm run lint               # tsc --noEmit (type-check only; no ESLint configured)
```

**The 95% rule:** almost every change is JS/TS — Metro reloads it onto the phone instantly. Only rebuild the dev-client APK when you touch `app.json` plugins, new `react-native-*` libraries, Android permissions, or new-arch flags. See `DEVELOPMENT.md` §"Two rebuild paths" for the local-vs-EAS decision.

## Distribution

EAS internal builds (no Play Store). Config: `eas.json`. Build profiles: dev-client (for development), internal (for stakeholders).

```bash
eas build --profile development --platform android
eas build --profile preview --platform android
```

## How it connects to the backend

Talks to `office-ops-engine`'s **inventory plugin** under `/api/inventory/*`. Base URL lives in `src/config.ts` (`EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` env override). Default in dev is the engine's ngrok tunnel.

Auth reuses the visitor module's **guard PIN flow**: `POST /api/guard/login` with `{ guardName, pin }` returns a session token that the field-app sends on every request as `x-guard-token`. `src/auth/session.ts` persists it; `src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx` exposes `useAuth()` + a live `useCan()` for RBAC gating. Gate the navigator on `session !== null` — unauthenticated users get the `LoginScreen` and nothing else.

Write paths go through the **outbox** (`src/db/outbox.ts`): the screen enqueues, the local SQLite cache is updated optimistically, then `flushOnce()` syncs each row to its dispatch in `sync/api.ts`. Read screens (`Stock`, `Alerts`, `Orders`) prefer remote on focus and fall back to local cache when offline. Every read screen calls `flushOnce()` before fetching remote so its first response reflects any just-queued writes.

## Conventions

- Offline-first: every write goes to local SQLite first, then queues for sync. Don't block UI on network.
- New native dependencies → bump version in `package.json`, then **rebuild the dev-client APK via EAS cloud** (`npx eas build --profile development --platform android`). This project does **not** use local Android Studio builds — no Java 17, no `ANDROID_HOME`, no `npm run android`. Skip `npm run prebuild` too — EAS runs prebuild on its servers, doing it locally is redundant. Once EAS finishes, install the APK on the phone, then `npm run start:dev-client` to serve JS.
- React Navigation (native-stack) for routing — not file-based.
- `react-native-reanimated` v4 is in use; remember the `'worklet'` directive for UI-thread functions.
- Don't introduce web-only libraries — anything DOM-specific will break the bundle.
- **Icons: Lucide only.** Use `lucide-react-native` components (`X`, `ScanLine`, `Check`, `AlertTriangle`, `Bell`, `Package`, `Truck`, `HandCoins`, `RefreshCw`, `Settings`, `Zap`/`ZapOff`, `Keyboard`, `Plus`/`Minus`, etc.). Pass them to `IconButton.Icon`, `Chip.Icon`, `StatusPill.Icon`, or inline as `<Icon size={N} color={palette.X} strokeWidth={2.2} />`. **Do not** use Unicode glyphs (`✓`, `⚠`, `←`, `⌖`, …) or emoji as action icons — they render inconsistently across fonts and at small sizes. Emoji is fine in user content (Hindi strings, vendor names) but not in chrome.
- **Theme + i18n + RBAC are provider-driven**, not module-level globals. Read from `useTheme()`, `useT()`, `useAuth()`/`useCan()`. The static `palette` re-export from `src/design/tokens.ts` is a fallback that mirrors the default theme — don't rely on it in new code.
- **Modules live in `src/modules/<id>/`** and self-register their screens via the module registry. Adding a new operational area (attendance, maintenance, …) means a new module folder + one line in `src/modules/registry.ts`, not edits to the navigator.
- **Loading UX**: list screens use `Skeleton` for first paint, not blank space. Refresh-on-focus does *not* re-show skeletons — keep existing rows visible while the background fetch runs. For the LLM normalizer's debounce, show an inline `ActivityIndicator` + "Checking…" hint so the user knows something is happening.

# office-ops-engine

The **central intelligence backend** for Office Ops Intelligence — the system that makes office operations smarter, more efficient, and future-proof. Everything operational flows through here.

> Root context: see `../CLAUDE.md` for the product vision, constraints (cost, user literacy, device capability, infrastructure), and how this subrepo fits the umbrella.

## What this service does

- Ingests messages and events from channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, web forms, PWAs) — channels are input adapters, not the product
- Classifies them into **domains** (visitor, inventory, maintenance, kitchen, ...)
- Extracts structured data with AI agents
- Routes work to **plugins** (bounded operational systems)
- Persists, syncs to Sheets, fans out notifications, surfaces overdue items
- Serves a REST/RPC API consumed by `ops-dashboard`, `visitor-web`, and `field-app`

Keep in mind: solutions built here must stay cheap to run (cost), simple to operate (literacy), and light on bandwidth/compute (device + infrastructure constraints). See root `CLAUDE.md` for the full constraint list.

Stack: **TypeScript + Mastra + Bun + Postgres + Drizzle + Pinecone**. Node `>=22.13.0`.

## Architectural vision (must read)

This subrepo has a canonical architecture doc — **read `ARCHITECTURE.md` before any structural change**. Summary:

- `src/mastra/core/` — channel-agnostic primitives (routing, scheduling, contracts). No WhatsApp/Telegram/visitor specifics here.
- `src/mastra/channels/` — thin adapters (telegram/, whatsapp/). Translate platform events to internal messages. No business logic.
- `src/mastra/domains/` — AI classification + extraction schemas. Not a dumping ground for general logic.
- `src/mastra/plugins/` — bounded operational systems (visitor, inventory, ...). Each owns its rules, routes, jobs, internal helpers. Expose a clean entrypoint; other code depends on that, not deep internals.
- `src/mastra/agents/`, `workflows/`, `tools/`, `scorers/` — Mastra primitives. **Register new ones in `src/mastra/index.ts`.**

The non-negotiable: **a new operational area (e.g. "kitchen orders") should be a new plugin + maybe a new domain, with minimal core changes.**

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev              # Mastra Studio at localhost:4111 (long-running, separate terminal)
npm run start:backend    # Run the bun HTTP server (port 4112)
npm run bot:dev          # Same with --watch
npm run build            # Production build
npm run dev:all          # Engine + dashboard + visitor-web concurrently
```

Tunnels (for exposing local to WhatsApp webhooks etc.):

```bash
npm run backendtunnel    # ngrok the backend (4112)
npm run visitortunnel    # ngrok the visitor PWA (5174)
npm run mastratunnel     # SSH-tunnel Mastra Studio
```

## Mastra-specific guardrails

- **Before any Mastra-related code change, load the `mastra` skill.** Mastra's APIs change between minor versions; cached knowledge is unreliable. The skill reads up-to-date docs from `node_modules`.
- Use Zod (or equivalent) schemas for every tool's input/output.
- Run `npm run build` to verify compilation after non-trivial changes.
- Don't modify `node_modules` or Mastra's internal DB files.

See `AGENTS.md` for the longer version of these rules.

## Deploy — read this before running `bifrost deploy`

This service deploys to Bifrost project **`auxilio-v2`**, env `dev`, service `ops-engine`. Public URL: `https://ops-engine-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site`.

**Always pass `--commit <full-sha>` explicitly.** Bifrost tags images as `<project-id>/<branch>:sha-<short>` at the **project** level. When two services share branch `main`, deploying one without `--commit` can pick up the other service's last image tag. Symptom we hit: the ops-dashboard URL served the visitor-web HTML. Sanity-check after deploy:

```bash
curl -s https://ops-engine-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site/health
```

Bifrost is wired to the `personal` remote (`junaid-appointy/office-ops-engine`), not `origin` (`AppointyIncubator/*`). Push to `personal main` before deploying.

Env is loaded from `office-ops-engine/env.updated` (not committed).

## Never do

- Commit `.env`, `env.updated`, or any `*.json` service-account credential files (e.g. `appointy-ops-*.json`, `auxilio-*.json` — already at repo root, treat as secrets).
- Hardcode API keys — always read from env.
- Put visitor-only / inventory-only logic in `core/` or `channels/`.
- Cross-import deep internal files of one plugin from another — go through the public entrypoint.
- Deploy without `--commit`.

## Pointers

- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — canonical architecture & boundaries
- `AGENTS.md` — Mastra rules
- `FLOW_PACK_GUIDE.md`, `Generalize_Flow_Editor.md` — flow-editor design notes
- `spec/`, `postman/` — API contracts and request collections
- `drizzle.config.ts`, `data/` — schema and seed data

# ops-dashboard

The **admin / leadership web dashboard** for Office Ops Intelligence. Used by office managers and team leads to see visitors, assets, inventory, maintenance state, and to configure flows. Part of the mission to make office operations smarter, more efficient, and future-proof.

> Root context: see `../CLAUDE.md` for the product vision and the four constraints (cost, literacy, device capability, infrastructure) that govern all design decisions.
> Backend it talks to: `../office-ops-engine/` (the intelligence layer).

## What this app does

- Surfaces structured operational data extracted by the backend
- Provides a **visual flow editor** (React Flow / `@xyflow/react` + dagre) for configuring extraction/routing flows without code
- Lets admins answer "who has laptop #23?", "what's open?", "who visited last week?" in seconds
- Read-mostly; mutations happen for flow config and ticket actions

Stack: **React 19 + Vite + TypeScript + TanStack Router + TanStack Query + PostHog + lucide-react**. Package manager: **bun** (lockfile is `bun.lock`).

## Commands

```bash
bun install
bun run dev        # Vite dev server, host 0.0.0.0
bun run build      # tsc -b && vite build
bun run preview    # preview built bundle
```

(`npm` also works — there's a `package-lock.json` too. Prefer `bun` for speed; either is fine.)

## How it connects to the backend

Talks to `office-ops-engine` via HTTP. Base URL comes from `VITE_OPS_API_URL`:

- **Local dev:** `http://localhost:4112`
- **Deployed dev:** `https://ops-engine-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site`

Other build-time env vars: `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY`, `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST`. All `VITE_*` vars are baked at build time — changing them requires a rebuild.

## Conventions

- TanStack Router uses file-based routing — add routes by adding files under the routes folder; the router regenerates types on dev.
- TanStack Query for all server state. **Don't introduce Redux / Zustand / Context for server data** — Query already handles cache, refetch, mutation.
- React 19 — server components are not in play here (Vite SPA), but the new hooks (`use`, `useActionState`) are available.
- The flow editor is the most complex screen; see `../React_Flow_Analysis.md` and `../Graph_Editor_Flow_Editor_Complete_Documentation.md` at repo root for design context.

## Deploy

Bifrost project **`auxilio-v2`**, env `dev`, service `ops-dashboard`. Public URL: `https://ops-dashboard-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site`. Built into an nginx container (see `Dockerfile`, `nginx-spa.conf.template`).

**Always pass `--commit <full-sha>` to `bifrost deploy`** (see umbrella `CLAUDE.md` and `office-ops-engine/CLAUDE.md` for the image-cross-serve incident). After deploying, sanity-check the served HTML title to make sure it's the dashboard, not visitor-web.

Build args required at deploy: `VITE_OPS_API_URL`, `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY`, `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST`.

Bifrost remote: `personal` → `junaid-appointy/office-ops-dashboard`. Push there.

## Verify UI changes before claiming done

This is a UI app — `tsc` passing does not mean the feature works. After non-trivial changes:

1. Start `bun run dev`.
2. Click through the golden path in a browser.
3. Check the network tab for failed API calls.
4. Watch for regressions on adjacent screens.

If you cannot run the browser (e.g. headless agent), say so explicitly. Do not claim the feature works.

content.text:
All four pieces done and type-clean. Summary of what shipped:

**field-app** (`field-app/`)
- New `EditStockScreen` (`src/modules/inventory/screens/EditStockScreen.tsx`) — opens with current qty + nearest expiry pre-filled, `QtyStepper` `min=0`, "No expiry" checkbox, Save disabled when nothing changed.
- StockScreen card now `onPress` → `navigation.navigate('EditStock', { barcode })` (`StockScreen.tsx:202`).
- New outbox kind `stock_correction` + dispatcher entry → `api.send.stockCorrection` → `POST /api/inventory/corrections`.
- New DB helpers `correctStockLocal`, `getNearestExpiry` (`src/db/stock.ts`).
- Registered in `inventoryModule.screens` + `RootStackParamList`. i18n keys: `editStock`, `editStockSub`, `currentCount`, `newCount`, `saveChanges`, `noChanges`.

**office-ops-engine** (`office-ops-engine/`)
- New table `inventory_stock_corrections` in `lib/postgres-schema.ts` (idempotent on `id`, FK to guards, indexed by site+date and site+barcode).
- New DB fns `insertStockCorrection`, `getStockCorrection`, `listStockCorrections`, `setStockOnHand` in `modules/inventory/db.ts`.
- New routes in `modules/inventory/routes.ts`:
  - `POST /api/inventory/corrections` — inserts audit row, overwrites `inventory_stock.on_hand` to the absolute new value, fires sheet append + debounced Stock-tab refresh.
  - `GET  /api/inventory/corrections` — list for dashboard.
- New `appendCorrectionRowToSheet` helper + `Corrections` headers added to `lib/google-sheets.ts` (date / time / product / barcode / old qty / new qty / Δ / old expiry / new expiry / corrected by).

**ops-dashboard** (`ops-dashboard/`)
- New `listStockCorrections` + `StockCorrectionRow` in `src/api/inventory.ts`.
- New **History** tab between Stock and Export in `InventorySection.tsx` — filterable table (product / barcode / guard) showing when, product, barcode, old→new qty + Δ, old→new expiry, performed by.

**Notes for testing:**
- I type-checked all three subrepos (only pre-existing visitor errors remain, unrelated to this work). I did **not** run the field-app on a device or the dashboard in a browser — please verify the UI flow yourself, especially: tap card → screen opens with correct qty + expiry, decrementing to 0 works, saving updates the stock count, and the History tab shows the row after a sync.
- Nothing deployed, nothing committed. Schema migration runs automatically on next engine boot (the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent and ships in the same `officeOpsSchemaSql()` block).

Done. The Edit Stock screen now mirrors the Receiving screen's expiry UX.

**What changed:**
- **field-app** `EditStockScreen.tsx`: added the `Different expiry per pack` toggle (only visible when qty > 1 and not "No expiry").   - `inventory_stock_corrections` table gains `new_expiries DATE[]` (with an idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` for already-deployed DBs).
  - `insertStockCorrection` hand-encodes the Postgres array literal and casts via `?::DATE[]`.
  - `getStockCorrection` / `listStockCorrections` flatten the array to a comma-separated string in the SELECT so the dashboard doesn't have to parse array unmarshalling.

content.text:
Found it. The bug is a missing sync.

**Diagnosis** (`CatalogPickerScreen.tsx:184-188`):

```ts
let barcode = incomingBarcode;
if (!barcode) {
  const existing = await findBarcodeForProduct(product.product_id);
  barcode = existing ?? `catalog_${product.product_id}`;
}
```

`findBarcodeForProduct` (`db/catalog.ts:84`) queries the **local** `product_barcodes` table. That table only gets a row when **this guard, on this device** scans a barcode and picks the matching catalog item (via the `learnBarcode(...)` call earlier in `pick`). It is **never populated from the backend**.

Look at the sync side (`sync/syncService.ts:122` `syncCanonicalProducts`): we pull `/api/inventory/canonical-products`, which gives each product a boolean `has_barcode` — but not the actual barcode value. So the device knows "this product has a barcode somewhere" but not what it is.

Result: if a barcode mapping was created by **another guard, by the admin in the dashboard, or via a bill upload**, this guard's local DB has no row in `product_barcodes` for it. `findBarcodeForProduct` returns `null`, so the code falls back to `catalog_<product_id>`, and `ReceivingScreen` shows "No barcode yet".

**Fix options:**

1. **Extend the catalog payload (recommended).** Add `primary_barcode` (most-recent learned) to the `RemoteCanonicalProduct` API response and cache it on `canonical_products`. `pick()` reads it from the catalog row instead of `product_barcodes`. One round-trip, no new endpoint, zero per-product DB calls. Tradeoff: only one barcode per product is surfaced — fine because the system enforces one-barcode-per-product today (the `has_barcode` flag already exists for the same reason).

2. **Sync `product_barcodes` as its own table.** Mirror the full server table into local SQLite each sync cycle. More correct if you ever allow multiple barcodes per product, but adds a sync step and table size grows with every learned mapping.

3. **On-pick lookup.** When the guard taps an item with `has_barcode=1` and no local row, fire a quick `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:id/barcode` and use that. Cheapest to ship but adds a network hop on every catalog pick — bad on patchy Wi-Fi, which violates the offline-first rule.

I'd ship **#1**. Want me to implement it? If yes, the change is: extend `RemoteCanonicalProduct`, add `primary_barcode` column to local `canonical_products` (migration to schema v7), populate it in `listCanonicalProducts` server-side, and switch `pick()` to read it.

Two separate things, only one is an app bug.

**HTTP 502 (one-off):** Server-side outage. Bifrost's proxy returned an HTML error page because `ops-engine` was down or restarting. Nothing for the field-app to fix; it correctly logged and moved on.

**HTTP 401 — "Invalid or expired session" (spamming):** Real bug. The guard's session token expired (or was revoked server-side), but the field-app **never clears the local session on a 401**. Look at the loop:

1. `flushOnce()` in `sync/syncService.ts:86` only skips backend pulls when `getSession()?.token` is null.
2. There's no global 401 handler in `sync/api.ts:46-64` — it just throws `ApiError`.
3. The caller (`syncCanonicalProducts`) catches it and logs a warning.
4. Token stays in `AsyncStorage`. Next sync tick (every `syncIntervalMs`) hits 401 again. Same with every network reconnect, every screen focus.

So you get one warning per sync tick, forever, until the user manually signs out — and meanwhile every outbox write also 401s and gets marked `failed`.

**Fix:** in `sync/api.ts`'s `request()`, detect status 401 and call `clearSession()`. Once the session is null, `flushOnce` skips reads, the `AuthProvider`'s `onSessionChange` listener fires, and `RootNavigator` re-renders into `LoginScreen` automatically (the gate at `RootNavigator.tsx:41` is already there). One-time fix; no extra plumbing needed.

Two small caveats worth deciding:

1. **Login endpoint itself returns 401 on bad PIN** — we must not clear the session in that case (there's no session to clear, but more importantly we don't want the side effect leaking into login). Easy: only clear when the request carried an `X-Guard-Token` header (i.e. `getSession()?.token` was set).
2. **Outbox rows mid-flush:** if a 401 hits during outbox dispatch, the rows get marked `failed`. After re-login, the user can manually retry from the Sync Queue UI. Acceptable for v1, or I can re-queue them automatically on session change — your call.

Want me to ship the fix (auto-clear on 401 + auto-redirect to Login)? And do you want failed-due-to-401 outbox rows auto-retried after re-login, or leave them in the manual queue?

content.text:
Here's the full picture of what's cached, where, and how it refreshes.

## What's cached

**Persistent SQLite tables** (survive app restart, wiped only by Settings → "Clear local data"):

| Table | Purpose | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| `canonical_products` | Product catalog (name, unit, pack_size, hsn, has_barcode, primary_barcode) | server → device |
| `product_barcodes` | barcode → product mappings | device-local (learned via scan) |
| `orders` + `order_items` | Open vendor orders | server → device |
| `stock_levels` | Per-product on_hand + nearest_expiry | server → device |
| `products` | Legacy locally-registered products | device-local |
| `receipts` | Captured receipts | device-local write log |
| `expiry_tracking` | Per-receipt expiry timeline | device-local write log |
| `activity_log` | Audit trail | device-local write log |
| `outbox` | Pending writes queue | device → server |

**AsyncStorage:**
- `@auxilio-session` — guard token + name + language (set on login, cleared on logout)
- `@auxilio-cache-time:<screen>` — last-fetch timestamp per screen namespace (catalog, stock, orders, alerts, home)
- Theme, i18n language

## When each cache refreshes

**On app boot** (`App.tsx:33`):
1. `getDb()` runs migrations.
2. `resetLocalCacheOnce()` wipes if a version sentinel changed.
3. `startSync()` — immediate `flushOnce()` + a 30-second timer + a network-reconnect listener.

**`flushOnce()` cycle** (every 30s while the app is open, plus on reconnect):
1. Recover any orphaned `sending` outbox rows.
2. Push the outbox batch.
3. **If logged in**, pull `canonical_products` (full replace) and open `orders`.
4. Stock is **not** pulled here — only on screen focus.

**On login** — and this is the gap worth calling out — there is **no eager fetch**. `login()` just stores the token. You then wait up to 30 seconds for the next `flushOnce()` tick to pull catalog + orders, and stock only loads when you open the Stock screen. This is why a freshly-logged-in user can stare at empty lists for half a minute.

**On screen focus** — each screen runs its own "stale?" check against `cacheTime.ts` (TTL = 30s):
- **StockScreen**: `flushOnce()` → if cache stale (>30s) `api.fetch.stock()` + `replaceStockFromRemote()`.
- **CatalogPickerScreen**: `useFocusEffect` → if cache stale, `syncCanonicalProducts()` + `syncOrders()`.
- **AlertsScreen / OrdersScreen / HomeScreen**: same pattern.
- **EditStockScreen / DispenseScreen / ReceivingScreen**: read local only, no fetch.

**Manual refresh:** pull-to-refresh on Stock/Orders/Alerts forces the fetch; "Sync Now" in the Outbox runs `flushOnce()`; the SyncRefreshButton on the Catalog Picker forces a catalog+orders pull.

**Never refreshed from server:**
- `receipts`, `expiry_tracking`, `activity_log` — these flow outbound only.
- `products` — legacy local-only table.
- `product_barcodes` — only populated by local `learnBarcode()`. Server-side mappings reach the device via `canonical_products.primary_barcode` (the fix we just shipped).

## The hole in the flow

The user-facing problem the question is hinting at: **login doesn't warm the cache**. Right now the flow is:

```
LoginScreen → setSession → Home renders → empty data for ~30s → first tick pulls catalog+orders → Stock screen still empty until you open it
```

The clean fix is to add a **post-login warm-up**: in `AuthProvider.login()`, after `setSession()`, await a one-shot `warmCache()` that runs in parallel:
- `syncCanonicalProducts()`
- `syncOrders()`
- `api.fetch.stock()` → `replaceStockFromRemote()`
- `api.fetch.alerts()` (optional — Alerts screen could keep its own fetch)

…and shows a "Loading…" or progress UI in place of letting the user reach an empty Home. If any of them fail, surface a recoverable error instead of silently leaving the cache empty.

Two design questions before I implement:

1. **Blocking vs. background:** block the user on the Login screen with a spinner until warm-up finishes? Or let them land on Home immediately and show per-tile skeletons until each piece arrives? I'd vote blocking (it's a one-time cost per session and avoids the "empty screen → suddenly populated" jank that's worse on low-end devices).

2. **Offline login:** if the warm-up fetch fails (no network), do we (a) refuse the login, (b) accept it and let the user work on stale local data, or (c) accept only if local cache exists, otherwise refuse? The current code accepts every login regardless, so (b) is least surprising; (c) is safer.

Want me to ship the warm-up? If yes, which option on each?

content.text:
Good — "plan first" is the right call here, this touches a lot. Here's the design.

## Principle: stale-while-revalidate + just-in-time verification

Two layers, both required:

- **Background freshness (cheap, runs on every focus):** render local cache instantly, always refetch in the background, smoothly swap. Screen is never blank if cache exists.
- **Just-in-time verification (the foolproof part):** for actions that *commit* state based on what the user is looking at (catalog pick, stock edit, dispense), do a single-row fetch right before the action. Without this, you can never guarantee freshness — a 1-second-old cache is still stale if the admin linked a barcode 500ms ago.

Background freshness gives a smooth UX. JIT verification is what makes it foolproof. Neither alone is enough.

## What changes, by area

### 1. Post-login warm-up (skeleton, not blocking)

In `AuthProvider.login()`, after `setSession()`:
- Fire `warmCache()` async (don't await — user lands on Home immediately).
- `warmCache()` = parallel `syncCanonicalProducts()` + `syncOrders()` + `api.fetch.stock()` + `api.fetch.alerts()`.
- Add a `useCacheStatus(key)` hook returning `'cold' | 'warm' | 'refreshing' | 'error' | 'offline'`. Home tiles + list screens render `Skeleton` for `cold`, real data otherwise. Already half-built — extend `cacheTime.ts` with a status field.

### 2. Drop the 30s TTL gate; always refetch on focus

`isCacheStale()` is the wrong primitive — it leads to "I just opened the screen, it's not stale yet, no fetch" which is exactly the bug class you want gone.

Replace with: every focus triggers a refetch. The TTL becomes a *throttle* (don't refetch if a fetch already fired <2s ago) instead of a *gate*. Result: open → see data → it refreshes → smooth swap.

Show a subtle "Refreshing…" indicator (existing SyncRefreshButton can spin) so the user knows something's happening but it doesn't block them.

### 3. Catalog picker — guaranteed-fresh pick

`CatalogPickerScreen`:
- On focus: render local cache + fire `syncCanonicalProducts()` always (per #2).
- **On `pick(product)`:** before navigating to ReceivingScreen, fire `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:id` (new single-row endpoint). Use that response's `primary_barcode`, `unit`, `pack_size`, `canonical_name` for the nav params.
- If the JIT fetch succeeds: navigate with verified data. The cached row was the visual hint; the freshly-fetched row is what actually commits.
- If the JIT fetch fails (offline / 5xx): show "Couldn't verify product — try again when online" and **block the pick**. Don't fall back to stale data, because that's how the bug you reported happens.

This is the single most important change for the no-barcode flow you described.

### 4. Stock and edit screens — JIT for the same reason

- **StockScreen** on focus: render local + refetch (per #2).
- **EditStockScreen** on open: render local `on_hand` + `nearest_expiry` immediately so the steppers don't lag, **and** fire a single-row `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode` in parallel. If the fetched count differs from local, show inline: "Stock has been updated to N since you opened this screen. Use new count? [Yes / Keep my edit]". User decides; nothing silently overwrites.
- **DispenseScreen** on item-select: same JIT fetch. Critical because dispensing 10 from a stock of 8 is a real bug.

### 5. Post-write invalidation (closes the 30s gap)

Right now if you dispense, the local cache reflects it (optimistic) but the next other-device sync waits up to 30s. We can't fix the *other* device without server push, but we can fix this device:

In `flushOnce()`, after a successful receipt/issue/correction, refetch the affected caches (stock for all three; orders for receipt). Means: after submitting, the next screen open sees the server's view, not just your optimistic write.

### 6. Connectivity-aware UX

- A thin global "Offline" banner when `Network.getNetworkStateAsync().isConnected === false`. Persistent until network returns.
- All JIT fetches fail-closed (block the action) when offline. Reads stay open from cache.
- Login already requires network (your rule #2). Add a clear error message ("Login needs internet") when the network call itself fails, distinct from "wrong PIN".

### 7. Auto-logout on 401 (the warning-spam fix from earlier)

Still needs to ship as part of this work. Any authed request that comes back 401 calls `clearSession()`. Without this, "stale data" includes "stale auth" and the warm-up loop spins forever.

### 8. Backend change required

One new endpoint:
- `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:productId` — single row with `has_barcode` + `primary_barcode` computed live (not cached). Used by the catalog picker's JIT verification.

The single-row stock endpoint already kind of exists via `findStock` but isn't exposed; needs `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode`. Trivial to add.

## What I'm explicitly NOT proposing now

- **WebSocket/SSE for server push.** This would eliminate the polling window entirely (server tells device "catalog changed, refetch"), but it's a real architecture change — auth on the socket, reconnection logic, fan-out from write paths. Worth doing when you outgrow polling; not today.
- **Incremental catalog sync** (only changed rows since last sync). Worth it when catalog crosses ~1k items. Today's full-replace is fine.
- **Cross-device awareness.** None of this fixes "Guard A on tablet sees stale data while Guard B on phone just dispensed". Only server push solves that. JIT verification on Guard A's *next action* catches it, which is the bar I think we're shooting for.

## State machine per cache

Every cache (`catalog`, `stock`, `orders`, `alerts`) carries one of:

```
cold        → never fetched this session → Skeleton
warm        → fetched once → show data, no indicator
refreshing  → warm + fetch in flight → show data + spinner
error       → last fetch failed → show data + retry banner
offline     → network down → show data + offline banner
```

Render is always non-blocking — `cold` is the only state that hides real content, and only because there's nothing to show.

## Risk: where this could break

- **JIT fetch latency on slow Wi-Fi.** Pick → 2-second wait → frustration. Mitigation: show a tiny inline spinner on the tapped row, time out at 3s, fall back to "Couldn't verify" message. Need to measure on actual warehouse Wi-Fi.
- **Server overhead.** Two extra single-row endpoints, hit once per pick / per edit-open. Should be fine; these are point-lookup queries on indexed columns. Worth verifying after wiring.
- **User who taps very fast.** Pick → JIT fires → user is already on ReceivingScreen by the time it comes back. Solution: don't navigate until JIT resolves (with the inline spinner). UX trade-off but it's the foolproof choice you asked for.

---

## Order of implementation (if you approve)

1. Backend: add `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:id` and `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode`.
2. Field-app: 401 auto-clear (kills the spam now).
3. Field-app: `warmCache()` on login + `useCacheStatus()` hook + Home/Stock skeletons.
4. Field-app: drop `isCacheStale` gate, replace with always-refetch-on-focus + throttle.
5. Field-app: JIT verification in CatalogPickerScreen `pick()`.
6. Field-app: JIT verification in EditStockScreen + DispenseScreen.
7. Field-app: post-write invalidation in `flushOnce()`.
8. Field-app: offline banner + JIT fail-closed when offline.

Each step is independently shippable and testable. I'd merge them as one logical change but build in this order so a partial state still works.

---

Three things to confirm before I start:

1. **JIT-blocking on pick:** spinner on the tapped row until the single-row fetch resolves, then navigate. You good with that small delay being the price of "guaranteed fresh"? (My recommendation: yes.)
2. **EditStock conflict prompt:** when the JIT fetch shows stock changed since you opened the screen, show an inline "Use new count? [Yes / Keep my edit]" prompt. Or just always show the latest and ditch the prompt?
3. **Offline reads:** today, screens show cached data with no warning when offline. After this work, do you want the offline banner *plus* a per-screen "Showing data from {timestamp}" line, or just the global banner?

# Field-app cache freshness plan

Goal: every screen always shows correct data, every action commits against current state, and the UX stays smooth on patchy warehouse Wi-Fi and low-end Android phones.

## Requirements (from product owner)

1. After login, let the user reach Home immediately — show skeletons while data loads. Do not block on warm-up.
2. Offline login is **not allowed**. Login requires a real server response.
3. The catalog list ("No barcode" path) must always reflect the latest server state without the user having to refresh or resync.
4. The Stock page (and every other data screen) must never show stale data.
5. Implementation must be foolproof — picking a stale item, dispensing against an outdated count, etc. must not be possible.

## Design principle: stale-while-revalidate + just-in-time verification

Two layers, both required:

- **Background freshness** — render the local cache instantly, always refetch in the background, smoothly swap. Screen is never blank if cache exists.
- **Just-in-time (JIT) verification** — for actions that *commit* state based on what the user is looking at (catalog pick, stock edit, dispense), fetch the single affected row right before the action. Without this, freshness can never be guaranteed: a 1-second-old cache is still stale if the admin changed something 500 ms ago.

Background freshness gives a smooth UX. JIT verification is what makes it foolproof. Neither alone is enough.

## What changes, by area

- Thin global "Offline" banner when `Network.getNetworkStateAsync().isConnected === false`. Persistent until network returns.

- Reads stay open from cache when offline (better than blank).

### 8. Backend changes required

Two new endpoints:

- `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:productId` — single row with live-computed `has_barcode` and `primary_barcode`. Used by catalog-picker JIT verification.
- `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode` — single stock row including the current nearest expiry. Used by EditStockScreen and DispenseScreen JIT verification.

Every cache (`catalog`, `stock`, `orders`, `alerts`) carries one of:

| State | Meaning | Render |
|---|---|---|
| `cold` | Never fetched this session | Skeleton |
| `warm` | Fetched once | Show data, no indicator |
| `refreshing` | Warm + fetch in flight | Show data + spinner |
| `error` | Last fetch failed | Show data + retry banner |
| `offline` | Network down | Show data + offline banner |

6. Field-app: JIT verification in `EditStockScreen` and `DispenseScreen` (with conflict prompt).
7. Field-app: post-write invalidation in `flushOnce()`.
8. Field-app: offline banner + JIT fail-closed when offline.

1. **JIT-blocking on catalog pick.** Spinner on the tapped row until the single-row fetch resolves, then navigate. Acceptable delay? *(Recommendation: yes — it's the price of "guaranteed fresh".)*
2. **EditStockScreen conflict prompt.** When JIT shows stock changed since the screen opened: show "Use new count? [Yes / Keep my edit]" prompt, **or** silently update to the latest value? *(Recommendation: prompt — user already had an intent.)*
3. **Offline reads UX.** Global "Offline" banner only, or also a per-screen "Showing data from {timestamp}" line? *(Recommendation: global banner only — per-screen line clutters the UI.)*

content.text:
Honest answer on all three.

## SSE — CPU and 100-user scale

**Idle CPU cost is negligible.** SSE = each client holds a long-lived HTTP/1.1 connection. On Bun/Node, an idle connection is one file descriptor in `epoll`/`kqueue`, one TLS session, and a few small JS objects. For 100 connections:

- ~10-50 MB RAM total
- <1% CPU at rest
- ~100 file descriptors

This is *nothing*. A single Bun/Node process can hold ~10k idle SSE connections comfortably. 100 is two orders of magnitude under that.

**The actual cost is the fan-out on writes.** When a receipt/dispense/correction is inserted, the server needs to push an event to every connected device on that site. Per push: ~200 bytes of JSON, sub-millisecond CPU.

Realistic load for you: roughly 200 writes/hour across 100 guards → 20,000 pushes/hour → ~5.5 pushes/second across all connections. Trivial.

Peak burst (a delivery being received, 50 scans in 2 minutes): without debouncing, 50 × 100 = 5000 pushes in 2 min. With **per-topic debouncing** (coalesce changes in a 500ms window into one "refetch hint"), it drops to ~10 × 100 = 1000 pushes. Still nothing.

**The cost is not what you'll trip on. Three other things are:**

1. **Bifrost ingress.** nginx/Cloudflare in front of `ops-engine` may buffer or close long-lived connections by default. Need `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, bumped `proxy_read_timeout`, and a heartbeat write every 15-30s to keep proxies happy. Must verify on Bifrost dev before committing to SSE.
2. **Multi-process pub/sub.** If `ops-engine` ever scales beyond one process (it's single right now), writes in process A must fan out to clients on process B. Cheapest backbone is **Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`** — you already have Postgres, no new infra. Redis pub/sub if you outgrow LISTEN/NOTIFY's payload limit (~8KB per notification).
3. **Reconnection storm.** When `ops-engine` restarts, all 100 clients reconnect simultaneously. Need jittered backoff on the client (random 0-5s delay before retry) to avoid hammering the server. Easy to add, easy to forget.

## SSE — will it handle 100 staff?

Yes, comfortably. Even 1000 would be fine on the current `ops-engine` footprint. The constraint isn't connection count, it's the items above (ingress config, pub/sub if you go multi-process, mobile reconnect logic).

**Mobile-specific gotchas:**

- React Native doesn't have a stock `EventSource`. You need `react-native-sse` (actively maintained, decent) or roll your own with `fetch` + `ReadableStream`. The first option is fine.
- Android suspends network when the app backgrounds. The connection will silently die after some seconds. You need to detect close and reconnect on foreground. SSE's built-in `Last-Event-ID` header lets the server replay missed events from a small in-memory buffer, so users don't miss anything during a 30s background.
- Token expiry on a long-lived stream. Server must close the stream with a clear reason code on 401-equivalent; client treats it the same as the polling 401 → clear session, kick to Login.
- Battery: SSE on Wi-Fi is essentially free. On cellular, the always-open socket prevents the radio from deep-sleeping, but it's still less battery than 30s polling.

## SSE — does it really fix cross-device staleness?

For **online** guards, yes. Guard B dispenses → server inserts → server emits `{ site_id, topic: "stock", barcode: "X" }` → Guard A's device receives within ms → device refetches stock for barcode X → screen updates.

For **offline** guards, no — they need JIT verification on their next action when they come back online. **SSE does not replace JIT.** It complements it:

- SSE closes the polling window for online users (the ~30s lag is gone).
- JIT closes the gap for offline users and for the narrow race between "I see fresh data" and "I commit an action" (which can still be milliseconds even with SSE).

You need both. The good news: with SSE in place, JIT fetches almost always return "no change" — it becomes a safety net, not the primary freshness mechanism.

## Incremental catalog sync — yes, easy

Backend: `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products?since=<ISO>` returns rows where `updated_at > since`. Client tracks the max `updated_at` from the last sync and sends it next time.

**Edge case to handle:** deletes. Full-replace catches them implicitly (rows missing from the response get dropped locally). Incremental sync misses them.

Two clean options:

1. **Periodic full-replace as reconciliation.** Run incremental sync most of the time; once an hour, run a full sync to catch deletes and recover from any drift.
2. **Tombstones.** Add `deleted_at` to `canonical_products`. Incremental sync returns soft-deleted rows so the client can drop them. Cleaner but needs a schema change and write-path edits.

I'd ship **#1** — it's a 5-line change on the client and zero schema work.

## Cost summary

| Feature | Backend cost | Mobile cost | Engineering effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| SSE for 100 users | Negligible | Slight battery hit on cellular; needs library + reconnect logic | 2-3 days focused + ~1 week soaking on real devices |
| Incremental catalog sync | One extra query column in WHERE | None | ~2 hours |
| Cross-device freshness without SSE | None extra | None | Not achievable without SSE/WebSocket |

## My recommendation

Ship the JIT verification plan first (steps 1-8 from the planning doc) — it's the foolproof layer and it works without SSE. Once that's solid and you've measured real warehouse Wi-Fi latency on JIT calls, layer SSE on top to eliminate the polling window. Incremental catalog sync can come in parallel; it's small and independent.

The risk with going SSE-first is that the mobile reconnect logic is genuinely tricky on Android, and if it's flaky, you've made freshness *worse* than the current polling. JIT gives you a correctness floor first, then SSE makes the UX feel real-time on top of that floor.

Want me to add an SSE section + the incremental-sync plan to the .md file?

6. **Write-path integration.** Every write path (receipt, issue, dispense, correction, catalog upsert, barcode learn) calls a small `emitChange(siteId, topic, payload)` helper after `COMMIT`. Topics: `stock`, `orders`, `catalog`, `alerts`. Payload is a hint only ("stock changed for barcode X"), not the new value — client refetches.
7. **Client dispatcher.** SSE messages invalidate the matching cache; TanStack-style "subscribe to topic" hook so screens auto-refetch when their topic fires.

| Concern | Cost |
|---|---|
| Server CPU idle | <1% |
| Server RAM | 10-50 MB for 100 connections |
| Mobile battery on Wi-Fi | Negligible (less than 30 s polling) |
| Mobile battery on cellular | Slight (radio can't deep-sleep) |
| Mobile data | Minimal — heartbeats + small JSON hints |
| Engineering effort | 2-3 days focused work + ~1 week soaking on real device fleet to shake out reconnect bugs |

### Real risks

- **Bifrost ingress closes streams.** Most common SSE deployment failure. Verify before commitment.
- **Reconnect storm on restart.** Without jittered backoff, all clients reconnect at once. Easy to add, easy to forget.
- **Flaky Android reconnect could make freshness WORSE than current polling.** This is why JIT ships first — it gives a correctness floor SSE can fail back to.
- **Token rotation mid-stream.** If guard PINs rotate or sessions expire on the server, mid-stream auth failures need a clean recovery path. Same handler as the 401 auto-clear.

## Phase 2: Incremental catalog sync

Trivial to add and orthogonal to the rest. Can ship in parallel with SSE.

- Backend: `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products?since=<ISO>` returns rows where `updated_at > since`.
- Client: track the max `updated_at` from the last sync; send it next time.

**Edge case: deletes.** Full-replace catches them implicitly (rows missing from the response get dropped locally). Incremental sync misses them.

Two options:

1. **Periodic full-replace as reconciliation.** Run incremental sync most of the time; once an hour, run a full sync to catch deletes and recover from any drift. *5-line client change, zero schema work.*
2. **Tombstones.** Add `deleted_at` to `canonical_products`; incremental sync returns soft-deleted rows so the client drops them. Cleaner but needs schema + write-path edits.

**Ship #1.** Move to #2 only if drift becomes a real problem at scale.

## Explicitly out of scope (still)

- **WebSocket** (vs SSE). SSE is one-way (server → client), which is exactly what we need (hints to refetch). WebSocket adds bidirectional capability we don't use, plus more reconnection complexity. Stick with SSE.
- **Server-side caching of catalog responses.** Premature optimisation; the queries are cheap.

# Field-app cache freshness plan

Goal: every screen always shows correct data, every action commits against current state, and the UX stays smooth on patchy warehouse Wi-Fi and low-end Android phones.

## Requirements (from product owner)

1. After login, let the user reach Home immediately — show skeletons while data loads. Do not block on warm-up.
2. Offline login is **not allowed**. Login requires a real server response.
3. The catalog list ("No barcode" path) must always reflect the latest server state without the user having to refresh or resync.
4. The Stock page (and every other data screen) must never show stale data.
5. Implementation must be foolproof — picking a stale item, dispensing against an outdated count, etc. must not be possible.

## Design principle: stale-while-revalidate + just-in-time verification

Two layers, both required:

- **Background freshness** — render the local cache instantly, always refetch in the background, smoothly swap. Screen is never blank if cache exists.
- **Just-in-time (JIT) verification** — for actions that *commit* state based on what the user is looking at (catalog pick, stock edit, dispense), fetch the single affected row right before the action. Without this, freshness can never be guaranteed: a 1-second-old cache is still stale if the admin changed something 500 ms ago.

Background freshness gives a smooth UX. JIT verification is what makes it foolproof. Neither alone is enough.

## What changes, by area

### 1. Post-login warm-up (skeleton, non-blocking)

In `AuthProvider.login()`, after `setSession()`:

- Fire `warmCache()` async (do not await — user lands on Home immediately).
- `warmCache()` = parallel:
  - `syncCanonicalProducts()`
  - `syncOrders()`
  - `api.fetch.stock()` → `replaceStockFromRemote()`
  - `api.fetch.alerts()`
- Add a `useCacheStatus(key)` hook returning one of: `'cold' | 'warm' | 'refreshing' | 'error' | 'offline'`.
- Home tiles and list screens render `Skeleton` for `cold`, real data otherwise.

### 2. Drop the 30 s TTL gate; always refetch on focus

`isCacheStale()` is the wrong primitive — it produces "I just opened the screen, cache isn't stale yet, no fetch" which is exactly the bug class we are eliminating.

Replace with:

- Every screen focus triggers a refetch.
- The TTL becomes a *throttle* (skip if a fetch fired in the last ~2 s) instead of a *gate*.
- Show a subtle "Refreshing…" indicator (the existing `SyncRefreshButton` can spin) so the user knows it's in flight, without blocking interaction.

### 3. Catalog picker — guaranteed-fresh pick (the no-barcode bug, properly fixed)

`CatalogPickerScreen`:

- On focus: render local cache + fire `syncCanonicalProducts()` always (per #2).
- **On `pick(product)`:** before navigating to `ReceivingScreen`, fire `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:productId` (new single-row endpoint).
  - Use the response's `primary_barcode`, `unit`, `pack_size`, `canonical_name` for the navigation params.
  - Show an inline spinner on the tapped row until the fetch resolves.
- If the JIT fetch succeeds → navigate with verified data.
- If the JIT fetch fails (offline / 5xx) → show "Couldn't verify product — try again when online" and **block the pick**. Never fall back to stale data.

This is the single most important change for the no-barcode flow.

### 4. Stock and edit screens — JIT for the same reason

- **StockScreen** on focus: render local + refetch (per #2).
- **EditStockScreen** on open:
  - Render local `on_hand` + `nearest_expiry` immediately so the steppers don't lag.
  - Fire `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode` in parallel.
  - If the fetched count differs from local, show inline: "Stock has been updated to N since you opened this screen. Use new count? [Yes / Keep my edit]".
- **DispenseScreen** on item-select: same JIT fetch before letting the user set qty. Dispensing 10 from a stock of 8 must not be possible.

### 5. Post-write invalidation (closes the 30 s gap)

Today, after a dispense/receipt/correction, the device sees its own optimistic write — but `flushOnce()` doesn't immediately refetch the affected caches.

Change: in `flushOnce()`, after a successful `receipt` / `issue` / `dispense` / `stock_correction`, refetch the affected caches (stock for all of them; orders for receipts).

Means: after the user submits, the next screen open already reflects the server's view, not just the optimistic write.

(This cannot fix *other* devices without server push; see "Explicitly out of scope" below.)

### 6. Connectivity-aware UX

- Thin global "Offline" banner when `Network.getNetworkStateAsync().isConnected === false`. Persistent until network returns.
- All JIT fetches **fail-closed** (block the action) when offline.
- Reads stay open from cache when offline (better than blank).
- Login already requires network. Add a clear "Login needs internet" error message, distinct from "wrong PIN".

### 7. Auto-logout on 401 (carries over from earlier)

Any authed request that returns 401 calls `clearSession()` in a central handler in `sync/api.ts`. Without this, "stale data" includes "stale auth", and the warm-up + polling loop spins 401-warnings forever (the bug already observed).

Skip the auto-clear when the request was login itself (no session to clear; only the LoginScreen surfaces the error).

### 8. Backend changes required

Two new endpoints:

- `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:productId` — single row with live-computed `has_barcode` and `primary_barcode`. Used by catalog-picker JIT verification.
- `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode` — single stock row including the current nearest expiry. Used by EditStockScreen and DispenseScreen JIT verification.

Both are point-lookup queries on indexed columns, cheap, no caching layer needed.

## State machine per cache

Every cache (`catalog`, `stock`, `orders`, `alerts`) carries one of:

| State | Meaning | Render |
|---|---|---|
| `cold` | Never fetched this session | Skeleton |
| `warm` | Fetched once | Show data, no indicator |
| `refreshing` | Warm + fetch in flight | Show data + spinner |
| `error` | Last fetch failed | Show data + retry banner |
| `offline` | Network down | Show data + offline banner |

Render is always non-blocking. `cold` is the only state that hides real content, and only because there is nothing to show.

## Risks and mitigations

- **JIT fetch latency on slow Wi-Fi.** Pick → 2 s wait → frustration.
  - Mitigation: inline spinner on the tapped row; time out at 3 s; on timeout show "Couldn't verify — try again". Measure on actual warehouse Wi-Fi before declaring this design final.
- **Extra server load.** Two extra single-row endpoints, hit once per pick / per edit-open. Should be fine; both are indexed point lookups. Verify after wiring.
- **Fast-tapping user.** Pick → JIT fires → user already navigated. Solution: do not navigate until JIT resolves. Spinner makes the delay legible.
- **Catalog growth (~1k+ items).** Full-replace sync gets slow at scale. Switch to incremental sync (`updated_at >`) when that happens.
- **Cross-device staleness.** Guard A sees stale data while Guard B just dispensed on another device. Only server push solves this fully. JIT verification on Guard A's *next action* catches it before it commits — that's the bar this plan reaches.

## Explicitly out of scope (for now)

- **WebSocket / SSE server push.** Would eliminate the polling window entirely (server tells device "catalog changed, refetch"), but it's a real architecture lift — auth on the socket, reconnection, fan-out from write paths. Revisit when polling stops being enough.
- **Incremental catalog sync.** Today's full-replace is fine. Move to delta sync when the catalog crosses ~1k items.
- **Eliminating cross-device staleness in real time.** See server push above.

## Implementation order

Each step is independently shippable and testable. Build in this order so a partial state still works:

1. Backend: add `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:id` and `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode`.
2. Field-app: 401 auto-clear in `sync/api.ts` (stops the warning spam now).
3. Field-app: `warmCache()` on login + `useCacheStatus()` hook + Home/Stock skeletons.
4. Field-app: drop `isCacheStale` gate; replace with always-refetch-on-focus + throttle; add "Refreshing…" indicator.
5. Field-app: JIT verification in `CatalogPickerScreen.pick()` (inline row spinner, fail-closed).
6. Field-app: JIT verification in `EditStockScreen` and `DispenseScreen` (with conflict prompt).
7. Field-app: post-write invalidation in `flushOnce()`.
8. Field-app: offline banner + JIT fail-closed when offline.

## Open decisions (need confirmation before implementing)

1. **JIT-blocking on catalog pick.** Spinner on the tapped row until the single-row fetch resolves, then navigate. Acceptable delay? *(Recommendation: yes — it's the price of "guaranteed fresh".)*
2. **EditStockScreen conflict prompt.** When JIT shows stock changed since the screen opened: show "Use new count? [Yes / Keep my edit]" prompt, **or** silently update to the latest value? *(Recommendation: prompt — user already had an intent.)*
3. **Offline reads UX.** Global "Offline" banner only, or also a per-screen "Showing data from {timestamp}" line? *(Recommendation: global banner only — per-screen line clutters the UI.)*

file.content:
# Field-app cache freshness plan

Goal: every screen always shows correct data, every action commits against current state, and the UX stays smooth on patchy warehouse Wi-Fi and low-end Android phones.

## Requirements (from product owner)

1. After login, let the user reach Home immediately — show skeletons while data loads. Do not block on warm-up.
2. Offline login is **not allowed**. Login requires a real server response.
3. The catalog list ("No barcode" path) must always reflect the latest server state without the user having to refresh or resync.
4. The Stock page (and every other data screen) must never show stale data.
5. Implementation must be foolproof — picking a stale item, dispensing against an outdated count, etc. must not be possible.

## Design principle: stale-while-revalidate + just-in-time verification

Two layers, both required:

- **Background freshness** — render the local cache instantly, always refetch in the background, smoothly swap. Screen is never blank if cache exists.
- **Just-in-time (JIT) verification** — for actions that *commit* state based on what the user is looking at (catalog pick, stock edit, dispense), fetch the single affected row right before the action. Without this, freshness can never be guaranteed: a 1-second-old cache is still stale if the admin changed something 500 ms ago.

Background freshness gives a smooth UX. JIT verification is what makes it foolproof. Neither alone is enough.

## What changes, by area

### 1. Post-login warm-up (skeleton, non-blocking)

In `AuthProvider.login()`, after `setSession()`:

- Fire `warmCache()` async (do not await — user lands on Home immediately).
- `warmCache()` = parallel:
  - `syncCanonicalProducts()`
  - `syncOrders()`
  - `api.fetch.stock()` → `replaceStockFromRemote()`
  - `api.fetch.alerts()`
- Add a `useCacheStatus(key)` hook returning one of: `'cold' | 'warm' | 'refreshing' | 'error' | 'offline'`.
- Home tiles and list screens render `Skeleton` for `cold`, real data otherwise.

### 2. Drop the 30 s TTL gate; always refetch on focus

`isCacheStale()` is the wrong primitive — it produces "I just opened the screen, cache isn't stale yet, no fetch" which is exactly the bug class we are eliminating.

Replace with:

- Every screen focus triggers a refetch.
- The TTL becomes a *throttle* (skip if a fetch fired in the last ~2 s) instead of a *gate*.
- Show a subtle "Refreshing…" indicator (the existing `SyncRefreshButton` can spin) so the user knows it's in flight, without blocking interaction.

### 3. Catalog picker — guaranteed-fresh pick (the no-barcode bug, properly fixed)

`CatalogPickerScreen`:

- On focus: render local cache + fire `syncCanonicalProducts()` always (per #2).
- **On `pick(product)`:** before navigating to `ReceivingScreen`, fire `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:productId` (new single-row endpoint).
  - Use the response's `primary_barcode`, `unit`, `pack_size`, `canonical_name` for the navigation params.
  - Show an inline spinner on the tapped row until the fetch resolves.
- If the JIT fetch succeeds → navigate with verified data.
- If the JIT fetch fails (offline / 5xx) → show "Couldn't verify product — try again when online" and **block the pick**. Never fall back to stale data.

This is the single most important change for the no-barcode flow.

### 4. Stock and edit screens — JIT for the same reason

- **StockScreen** on focus: render local + refetch (per #2).
- **EditStockScreen** on open:
  - Render local `on_hand` + `nearest_expiry` immediately so the steppers don't lag.
  - Fire `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode` in parallel.
  - If the fetched count differs from local, show inline: "Stock has been updated to N since you opened this screen. Use new count? [Yes / Keep my edit]".
- **DispenseScreen** on item-select: same JIT fetch before letting the user set qty. Dispensing 10 from a stock of 8 must not be possible.

### 5. Post-write invalidation (closes the 30 s gap)

Today, after a dispense/receipt/correction, the device sees its own optimistic write — but `flushOnce()` doesn't immediately refetch the affected caches.

Change: in `flushOnce()`, after a successful `receipt` / `issue` / `dispense` / `stock_correction`, refetch the affected caches (stock for all of them; orders for receipts).

Means: after the user submits, the next screen open already reflects the server's view, not just the optimistic write.

(This cannot fix *other* devices without server push; see "Explicitly out of scope" below.)

### 6. Connectivity-aware UX

- Thin global "Offline" banner when `Network.getNetworkStateAsync().isConnected === false`. Persistent until network returns.
- All JIT fetches **fail-closed** (block the action) when offline.
- Reads stay open from cache when offline (better than blank).
- Login already requires network. Add a clear "Login needs internet" error message, distinct from "wrong PIN".

### 7. Auto-logout on 401 (carries over from earlier)

Any authed request that returns 401 calls `clearSession()` in a central handler in `sync/api.ts`. Without this, "stale data" includes "stale auth", and the warm-up + polling loop spins 401-warnings forever (the bug already observed).

Skip the auto-clear when the request was login itself (no session to clear; only the LoginScreen surfaces the error).

### 8. Backend changes required

Two new endpoints:

- `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:productId` — single row with live-computed `has_barcode` and `primary_barcode`. Used by catalog-picker JIT verification.
- `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode` — single stock row including the current nearest expiry. Used by EditStockScreen and DispenseScreen JIT verification.

Both are point-lookup queries on indexed columns, cheap, no caching layer needed.

## State machine per cache

Every cache (`catalog`, `stock`, `orders`, `alerts`) carries one of:

| State | Meaning | Render |
|---|---|---|
| `cold` | Never fetched this session | Skeleton |
| `warm` | Fetched once | Show data, no indicator |
| `refreshing` | Warm + fetch in flight | Show data + spinner |
| `error` | Last fetch failed | Show data + retry banner |
| `offline` | Network down | Show data + offline banner |

Render is always non-blocking. `cold` is the only state that hides real content, and only because there is nothing to show.

## Risks and mitigations

- **JIT fetch latency on slow Wi-Fi.** Pick → 2 s wait → frustration.
  - Mitigation: inline spinner on the tapped row; time out at 3 s; on timeout show "Couldn't verify — try again". Measure on actual warehouse Wi-Fi before declaring this design final.
- **Extra server load.** Two extra single-row endpoints, hit once per pick / per edit-open. Should be fine; both are indexed point lookups. Verify after wiring.
- **Fast-tapping user.** Pick → JIT fires → user already navigated. Solution: do not navigate until JIT resolves. Spinner makes the delay legible.
- **Catalog growth (~1k+ items).** Full-replace sync gets slow at scale. Switch to incremental sync (`updated_at >`) when that happens.
- **Cross-device staleness.** Guard A sees stale data while Guard B just dispensed on another device. Only server push solves this fully. JIT verification on Guard A's *next action* catches it before it commits — that's the bar this plan reaches.

## Phase 2: SSE for real-time freshness

JIT verification (above) gives a correctness floor. SSE on top of it eliminates the polling window and makes the UX feel real-time. **Ship JIT first**, measure real-Wi-Fi latency, then layer SSE.

### Will it scale to 100 staff?

Yes, comfortably. Idle SSE connection cost is essentially zero:

- Each connection: ~one file descriptor, one TLS session, a small JS object, a periodic heartbeat write.
- 100 connections: ~10-50 MB RAM total, <1% CPU at rest.
- A single Bun/Node process holds ~10k idle SSE connections without straining. 100 is two orders of magnitude under that.

The real cost is **fan-out on writes**. Realistic load:

- ~200 writes/hour across 100 guards → ~20k pushes/hour → ~5.5 pushes/second. Each push ~200 bytes JSON, sub-ms CPU. Trivial.
- Peak burst (delivery scan, 50 receipts in 2 minutes): without debouncing 5000 pushes; with per-topic debouncing (coalesce changes in a 500 ms window into one "refetch hint") drops to ~1000. Still nothing.

### What it does NOT fix

SSE only helps **online** guards. Offline guards still need JIT verification on their next action when they reconnect. **SSE complements JIT; it does not replace it.** With SSE in place, JIT fetches usually return "no change" and become a safety net instead of the primary freshness mechanism.

### What we need to do for SSE

1. **Pub/sub backbone.** Use Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` — already have Postgres, no new infra. Move to Redis if a notification ever needs to be >8 KB (it won't for our hint-only events). Required if `ops-engine` ever scales beyond one process; cheap to do upfront anyway.
2. **Bifrost ingress configuration.** Verify SSE survives the proxy. Required:
   - `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (response header)
   - `Cache-Control: no-cache` (response header)
   - Bumped `proxy_read_timeout` on the ingress
   - Heartbeat write every 15-30 s to keep proxies from closing the stream
   - Must be tested on Bifrost dev before committing.
3. **Mobile client.** `react-native-sse` (actively maintained) or a hand-rolled `fetch` + `ReadableStream`. The first is fine.
4. **Reconnect logic.**
   - **Jittered backoff** on reconnect (random 0-5 s) — prevents 100 clients hammering the server simultaneously when `ops-engine` restarts.
   - **Foreground reconnect** — Android suspends network when the app backgrounds; the connection silently dies. Detect on foreground and reconnect.
   - **`Last-Event-ID` resume** — server keeps a small in-memory ring buffer of recent events per site; on reconnect the client sends `Last-Event-ID` and server replays anything missed in the gap. Prevents missed events during ~30 s backgrounding.
5. **Auth on the stream.** Carry the session token in the URL or initial connect. On token expiry, server closes the stream with a recognisable reason; client treats it like the polling 401 — clear session, kick to Login.
6. **Write-path integration.** Every write path (receipt, issue, dispense, correction, catalog upsert, barcode learn) calls a small `emitChange(siteId, topic, payload)` helper after `COMMIT`. Topics: `stock`, `orders`, `catalog`, `alerts`. Payload is a hint only ("stock changed for barcode X"), not the new value — client refetches.
7. **Client dispatcher.** SSE messages invalidate the matching cache; TanStack-style "subscribe to topic" hook so screens auto-refetch when their topic fires.

### What it costs

| Concern | Cost |
|---|---|
| Server CPU idle | <1% |
| Server RAM | 10-50 MB for 100 connections |
| Mobile battery on Wi-Fi | Negligible (less than 30 s polling) |
| Mobile battery on cellular | Slight (radio can't deep-sleep) |
| Mobile data | Minimal — heartbeats + small JSON hints |
| Engineering effort | 2-3 days focused work + ~1 week soaking on real device fleet to shake out reconnect bugs |

### Real risks

- **Bifrost ingress closes streams.** Most common SSE deployment failure. Verify before commitment.
- **Reconnect storm on restart.** Without jittered backoff, all clients reconnect at once. Easy to add, easy to forget.
- **Flaky Android reconnect could make freshness WORSE than current polling.** This is why JIT ships first — it gives a correctness floor SSE can fail back to.
- **Token rotation mid-stream.** If guard PINs rotate or sessions expire on the server, mid-stream auth failures need a clean recovery path. Same handler as the 401 auto-clear.

## Phase 2: Incremental catalog sync

Trivial to add and orthogonal to the rest. Can ship in parallel with SSE.

- Backend: `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products?since=<ISO>` returns rows where `updated_at > since`.
- Client: track the max `updated_at` from the last sync; send it next time.

**Edge case: deletes.** Full-replace catches them implicitly (rows missing from the response get dropped locally). Incremental sync misses them.

Two options:

1. **Periodic full-replace as reconciliation.** Run incremental sync most of the time; once an hour, run a full sync to catch deletes and recover from any drift. *5-line client change, zero schema work.*
2. **Tombstones.** Add `deleted_at` to `canonical_products`; incremental sync returns soft-deleted rows so the client drops them. Cleaner but needs schema + write-path edits.

**Ship #1.** Move to #2 only if drift becomes a real problem at scale.

## Explicitly out of scope (still)

- **WebSocket** (vs SSE). SSE is one-way (server → client), which is exactly what we need (hints to refetch). WebSocket adds bidirectional capability we don't use, plus more reconnection complexity. Stick with SSE.
- **Server-side caching of catalog responses.** Premature optimisation; the queries are cheap.

## Implementation order

Each step is independently shippable and testable. Build in this order so a partial state still works.

### Phase 1 — JIT + warm-up (correctness floor)

1. Backend: add `GET /api/inventory/canonical-products/:id` and `GET /api/inventory/stock/:barcode`.
2. Field-app: 401 auto-clear in `sync/api.ts` (stops the warning spam now).
3. Field-app: `warmCache()` on login + `useCacheStatus()` hook + Home/Stock skeletons.
4. Field-app: drop `isCacheStale` gate; replace with always-refetch-on-focus + throttle; add "Refreshing…" indicator.
5. Field-app: JIT verification in `CatalogPickerScreen.pick()` (inline row spinner, fail-closed).
6. Field-app: JIT verification in `EditStockScreen` and `DispenseScreen` (with conflict prompt).
7. Field-app: post-write invalidation in `flushOnce()`.
8. Field-app: offline banner + JIT fail-closed when offline.

### Phase 2 — SSE + incremental sync (real-time + scale)

Only after Phase 1 has soaked in production for at least a week.

9. Backend: incremental catalog sync (`?since=<ISO>` + hourly full reconciliation). *Cheap; can ship in parallel with the rest of Phase 1.*
10. Backend: verify SSE survives Bifrost ingress (`X-Accel-Buffering`, `proxy_read_timeout`, heartbeats). **Block on this** — if it doesn't work through the proxy, SSE is dead before it starts.
11. Backend: `emitChange(siteId, topic, payload)` helper; wire into every write path after `COMMIT`. Topics: `stock`, `orders`, `catalog`, `alerts`. Hint-only payloads.
12. Backend: SSE endpoint `GET /api/inventory/events?token=...&siteId=...` with Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` backbone, in-memory ring buffer for `Last-Event-ID` resume, heartbeats every 15 s.
13. Field-app: `react-native-sse` client with jittered backoff, foreground reconnect, `Last-Event-ID` resume.
14. Field-app: client dispatcher — SSE topic → invalidate matching cache → screens auto-refetch via existing focus path.
15. Field-app: tear down the 30 s polling timer once SSE is proven on the device fleet. Keep it as a fallback for the first 2-4 weeks of soak.

## Open decisions (need confirmation before implementing)

1. **JIT-blocking on catalog pick.** Spinner on the tapped row until the single-row fetch resolves, then navigate. Acceptable delay? *(Recommendation: yes — it's the price of "guaranteed fresh".)*
2. **EditStockScreen conflict prompt.** When JIT shows stock changed since the screen opened: show "Use new count? [Yes / Keep my edit]" prompt, **or** silently update to the latest value? *(Recommendation: prompt — user already had an intent.)*
3. **Offline reads UX.** Global "Offline" banner only, or also a per-screen "Showing data from {timestamp}" line? *(Recommendation: global banner only — per-screen line clutters the UI.)*
